transcript:
Header: 2026-11-10 15:00 UTC | Duration: ~45m | Attendees: Maya, Ravi (Redwood) + Emily, Carlos, Aisha, Tom (NexaHealth)

00:00 Maya: Okay everyone, thanks for joining, this is Maya from Redwood, we'll do the usual quick sync — status on onboarding, env readiness, any blockers.
00:06 Emily: Hey, yes thanks, we have a couple of items, main one is VPC peering still pending, and then we want to confirm KV cache behavior with our long context chats.
00:15 Ravi: Great, yeah I can cover the staging details and some quick tuning tips. Quick note, sorry if transcription messes up names — sometimes our product name gets weird, we'll try to be clear.
01:05 Carlos: On peering, I raised the ticket with infra but the security team wants to review the route tables and NAT egress. Aisha will chime in.
01:12 Aisha: Yes, we need to ensure KMS integration meets our policy — we don't want keys stored outside our HSM and we need audit log retention for 1 year.
01:22 Maya: That's fair; Redwood supports customer-managed keys and we've done HSM integrations with a few customers. I'll attach our KMS integration doc after the call.
01:29 Tom: Also curious about dedicated vs hosted for the pilot, cost tradeoffs — we just want to prove quality and latency.
01:40 Ravi: For a pilot, hosted with pinned model variant is simplest. But if you want predictable p99 latency we can spin up a small dedicated pool; it depends on traffic pattern.
02:05 Emily: Our traffic for the pilot will be small, like 100-200 reqs/min but with long contexts up to 6k tokens. Latency target is 800ms p95 ideally, and cost is also a concern.
02:18 Ravi: With long context you'll see higher latency; we can recommend quantization + prefix caching. For the stage we'll run a 1k request benchmark to capture distributions.
03:02 Carlos: One question: will the staging environment need full VPC peering or can we do a temporary public endpoint with IP allowlisting?
03:12 Ravi: We can do either. For speed, you can use a staging API key with IP allowlist and restrict data, then later switch to VPC peering for production. There is a small security tradeoff.
03:30 Aisha: IP allowlisting is okay for the pilot if logs are kept and keys rotated. But we need to see proof of encryption in transit + at rest.
03:42 Maya: We'll include the TLS and storage encryption details in the docs.
04:10 Emily: About logs — we will need request-level audit logs; are those available in Redwood console?
04:18 Maya: Yes, we have per-request tracing and token-level cost breakdowns in the console. For private deployments we can push logs to your splunk/s3 — we'll show the options in the security pack.
05:00 Tom: There was a note in the onboarding doc about a 'Redwood verified' model catalog — is that a hosted-only feature?
05:10 Ravi: The verified profiles are curated, yes, but we can deploy the same model variant on dedicated or private if licensing allows.
05:30 Emily: Okay good.
06:00 Maya: Quick status recap — action items from our side: I'll send SOC2 and ISO certs, KMS integration notes, and the short guide for IP allowlist. Ravi will provision staging service account and a quickstart to run the benchmark.
06:20 Carlos: We will try to unblock infra to allow IP egress for the test, if not we'll aim for VPC peering. Expect an update by EOD tomorrow.
07:00 Emily: On quality metrics, we'll share 200 prompt-response pairs and our scoring rubric. We want to avoid regressions vs current baseline.
07:12 Ravi: Great — we'll run evals and surface any regressions via the Redwood Optimize eval harness.
08:30 Aisha: On compliance, two specific asks: 1) can logs be redacted before leaving our VPC, 2) do you have SOC2 Type II?
08:42 Maya: Yes, SOC2 Type II — doc coming. On redaction, with private deployment you can keep logs inside your network; with hosted we offer field redaction and a retention config.
09:05 Tom: Anything around SSO/SSP? We use Okta, want SAML SSO and RBAC mapping.
09:14 Maya: We support SAML/Okta and SCIM for provisioning. We'll include sample metadata and mapping.
10:00 Carlos: Back to perf, for 6k token context are you using KV cache or chunking? We saw some weird token growth.
10:10 Ravi: Redwood runtime uses KV cache for streaming contexts, but long prompt windows can increase memory. For the pilot we recommend 8-bit quantization with prefix caching and we can tune batch sizes.
11:00 Emily: Any quick numbers to expect for p95 on 6k tokens on a single GPU?
11:10 Ravi: Very roughly, on an A100-type GPU maybe 1.2-1.8s p95 depending on model size and kernel optimizations. We'll run exact numbers in the benchmark.
12:00 Aisha: One more around data residency — our data must stay in eu-west-1 for pilot production later. For now staging in us-east is ok?
12:10 Maya: Staging in us-east is fine for now; for production we can pin region. We'll note that in the rollout doc.
13:20 Emily: Ok so immediate checklist: security docs, staging access, example workloads, and schedule latency tune session.
14:00 Maya: Yep — also we'll provide a short runbook for test harness and a shared spreadsheet to collect benchmark results.
15:05 Tom: Do you have a sample cost estimate for 100 reqs/min with 6k token avg? We'd like a ballpark to include in our POC budget.
15:20 Ravi: Ballpark hosted could be X per 1k tokens (we'll put numbers in the pricing sheet), for dedicated you'd have a monthly commit which might be cheaper at scale. We'll send a sample cost comparison.
16:00 Emily: Any blockers right now that will stop the pilot starting next week?
16:06 Carlos: VPC peering could, but we aim to work around with IP allowlist. I'll confirm by tomorrow.
17:00 Aisha: We also want to validate KMS flows; we'll need Redwood sample key rotation timeline to review.
17:10 Maya: We'll include rotation SLAs and integration notes.
18:00 Maya: Ok let's recap next steps — I'll send security package and SAML example by Thursday 11/12; Ravi provision staging account and upload quickstart by Monday 11/15; Emily to send sample prompts and acceptance criteria by 11/13; Carlos to confirm network approach by 11/11.
18:40 Emily: Sounds good. Also please share the benchmark spreadsheet link when available.
19:00 Maya: Will do. Thanks everybody, we'll follow up in Slack/email and reconvene next week same time.
19:30 call ends
